At this time, the Earth was still a small, rocky planet, and it was surrounded by a large disk of debris, including small rocks and dust. This debris disk was likely the result of collisions between smaller bodies in the solar system.

One of the most massive objects in the solar system at this time was a Mars-sized planet called Theia. Theia is thought to have formed in the same region of the solar system as the Earth, and it's believed to have been a terrestrial planet, similar in composition to the Earth.
